_status: DRAFT. Every value must be clinician-verified against the cited source before entering a build. Fields marked _verify:true are not yet confirmed.

prototype.label: PROTOTYPE ONLY - unverified clinical guideline pack may execute only in explicitly labelled prototype builds.

source: WHO/UNICEF 2012 pneumonia/diarrhoea materials; WHO/UNICEF 2004 acute-diarrhoea statement; WHO 2019 sick-young-infant chart booklet and participant manual; WHO IMCI fever module; Bangladesh EPI (DGHS).

ari._note: IMCI fast-breathing thresholds drive the Respiration Timer's rate check.

respiratoryRate._note: A counted rate below this is treated as a failed count, not as a reading, and the caregiver is asked to count again. There is deliberately no maximum: refusing a high count could hide the fast-breathing sign.
respiratoryRate._source: prototype safety floor; not an IMCI threshold

diarrhoea.persistent_source: WHO IMCI: diarrhoea lasting 14 days or more is PERSISTENT DIARRHOEA. With dehydration it is SEVERE PERSISTENT DIARRHOEA and is referred. Without dehydration it still needs facility assessment, feeding counselling, and follow-up in 5 days, and a child under 6 months is referred.
diarrhoea.persistent_provenance: Added 2026-08-25. The app already asked how many days the diarrhoea had lasted and passed diarrhoea_days into the engine, but no predicate or rule read it, so the answer changed nothing. David, 2026-08-25: 'does the IMCI who guidelines say long diarrhea goes to clinic? If so, add to our rules.'

perLooseStool._source: WHO/UNICEF: after each loose stool give 50-100 mL to a child under 2 years and 100-200 mL to a child aged 2 years or more
perLooseStool._provenance: These amounts and the 24-month cut-off were hardcoded in apps/pwa-sandbox/ui-core.js until 2026-08-20. Moved here so the band a caregiver is shown is a governed number rather than a literal in a render function.

zinc._source: WHO/UNICEF joint statement 2004; reaffirmed UNICEF 2012 report

dangerSigns: sunken eyes / signs of severe dehydration

antibiotics._note: The 'no antibiotics' voucher renders ONLY when there is no blood in stool AND no danger sign.

voucher.en: MOH guidance: my child needs ORS and zinc. No antibiotics needed.

immunization._note: Bangladesh EPI schedule. Populate + verify against DGHS/EPI Bangladesh and WHO-UNICEF coverage estimates.

malaria.note: Country/localizer policy controls whether malaria testing is relevant. Test validity is deliberately unresolved until the national protocol is approved.
malaria._source: WHO IMCI fever pathway; national malaria protocol required

fever._source: WHO IMCI fever module; persistent-no-improvement timing is prototype product policy pending review
fever._provenance: Axillary site only; no offset is inferred for oral, rectal, ear, or forehead readings

young_infant._source: WHO 2019 sick young infant chart booklet and participant manual
young_infant._provenance: Clinical young-infant band is 0-59 completed days; this does not redefine the app newborn persona

anc._source: WHO 2016 recommendations on antenatal care for a positive pregnancy experience: eight contacts at 12, 20, 26, 30, 34, 36, 38 and 40 weeks
anc._provenance: Used only to pace the antenatal comic series and to say which contact a mother is near. No clinical advice is derived from these weeks; the schedule a mother should follow is whatever her local programme runs.
